column8: Charon has the same spirit; KSF leak_guard could be ported as a strict pattern gate.

column3: Code that is built and unit-tested but never actually called from any wired path is flagged
column8: Charon no inert_code detector; this would catch the built-but-not-wired class (same disease as the gap this ticket addresses).

column3: Every rule is classified mechanized/guidance/GAP; goal = 100% mechanized; 8-class gap taxonomy
column8: Charon no enforcement-coverage SSOT; this register is the start but not yet a meta-gate.

column3: Every module is wired with correct gates, tests, and surface; module.toml gates list is enforced
column8: Charon no module.toml contract; could adopt a lightweight variant for fleet/checks/.

column3: Before building new code, run reuse-check against the candidate path; if similar code exists, reuse it
column8: Charon has fleet/reuse-check.sh as a one-command wrapper around ksf reuse-check.

column3: Every gate runs a verify-self pass that exercises the gate against known inputs and confirms expected outcomes
column8: Charon tests/*.test.sh are the structural equivalent; KSF's formal verify_self is a tighter contract.

column3: Each module declares: name, surface (path GLOB), gates (list), entrypoints (list)
column8: Charon no module.toml equivalent; could apply to fleet/checks/*.sh as the gate-registry unit.

column3: Each module must have test_redproof.py proving the gate CAN go red
column8: Charon *.test.sh is the bash equivalent; same intent.

column3: Adding a new gate pattern is a registry entry, not a new gate script; the gate code reads patterns from data
column8: Charon has no pattern-registry; this is the anti-accretion generalization. SESSION-HANDOFF-mace-windu notes KS28 as a designed next.

column3: Single-command merge/land wrapper: commit pending → run gate (refuse-on-red) → branch → push → open+merge PR → sync local base. Refuses ungated merges.
column8: SLOP-TICKET: land.sh-equivalent — wrap ms-enforce + git push in a single refuse-on-red script; mediastack has Makefile targets but not a refuse-on-red gate before push.

column3: Lever-gated push wrapper: checks AUTONOMOUS state; if ON pushes without asking, if OFF asks first. Raw git push deny-listed.
column8: SLOP-TICKET: lift_push_restore analog that respects a lever/session-state for unattended vs supervised mode. SLOP has lift_push_restore.py; lever-gating is the new piece.

column3: Pre-handoff gate: every referenced SHA/path/script in the handoff must exist; committed-SHA claim must be real. Non-zero exit = incomplete handoff.
column8: SLOP-TICKET: ms-enforce check_handoff_facts equivalent with file-existence + SHA-grep verification. The mechanism is in SLOP but not committed to a fail-closed gate.

column3: Mechanized board validator: flags tickets missing Dependencies & Sequence; flags orphan tickets (not in any project); flags stale parked items.
column8: SLOP-TICKET: validate_board analog for tracking.db — required-fields at claim time; orphan detection; freshness-signal-to-red for parked items.

column3: Verifies a ticket's file ownership is disjoint from other in-flight tickets; non-disjoint tickets must declare a serialization or stay serial.
column8: KSF-TICKET: wci-contention.sh analog for KSF modules — a gate that verifies two in-flight modules don't share surface. KSF has reuse_check; parallelizability is the missing axis.

column3: Before any build, gate that the ticket's base contains its prereq commits; never build on stale base.
column8: KSF-TICKET: base-integrity check as a ksf gate — gate that a module's expected prereq gates are present in the base before building. KSF module.toml could carry base-prereqs field.

column3: Hard block on any work executor invoking `claude -p` or `claude --bg`. Work runs off-Claude via gateway.
column8: SLOP-TICKET: provider-agnostic executor check — block any single-vendor hardcode in the executor. Same family as audit_single_entity_hardcode but executor-scoped.

column3: Per-project pre-build audit: enumerate wave tickets, code-confirm BUILT/PARTIAL/STUB/NOT-STARTED with file:line, surface false blockers and pull-up candidates.
column8: SLOP-TICKET: project-start-audit.sh equivalent — before opening a wave, code-confirm every ticket; surface stale docstrings (the GAP-REGISTER manual-cherry-pick class is the exact miss this prevents).

column3: File-contention axis: flags >=N-owner files so the decomposer can re-shape around them.
column8: KSF-TICKET: wci-contention for ksf/modules — multi-owner surface file flag, feeds the decompose_sizing tool. KSF has reuse_check; contention-axis is missing.

column3: Capability-based cost-tier registry: providers are bucketed by capability + cost_class; routing reads the registry, never hardcodes providers.
column8: SLOP-TICKET: cost_class registry analog — auto-derive cost_class from captured pricing + manual overrides; never hardcode a provider's class in the executor. Auto-derives the SR-12 'auto cost_rank from pricing' ticket idea.

column3: Single source of truth for roadmap display: Projects → Waves → tickets, verbatim from ROADMAP.tsv. No editorialization, no summary.
column8: SLOP-TICKET: roadmap-display gate — block any summary/rollup that preempts the canonical report. SLOP has ms-status but no equivalent 'always-raw' discipline.

column3: Handoff generator: machine-state block (live SHAs, ticket state, open blockers) is derived, not typed; handoff-check.sh gates accuracy.
column8: SLOP-TICKET: SESSION-HANDOFF.md generator that derives the state block (true_state.py equivalent); SLOP has tools/true_state.py and tools/handoff_facts.py; wire them into the canonical handoff generator.

column3: Roadmap/board surfaced at SessionStart hook — every session sees the live state without re-deriving.
column8: SLOP-TICKET: SessionStart hook that runs ms-status + report + board; eliminate per-session re-derivation of the live state.

column3: Per-ticket review-log fragment instead of shared-append. Eliminates droid-vs-droid collision on REVIEW-LOG.md.
column8: SLOP-TICKET: per-ticket REVIEW-LOG fragments — eliminate the shared docs/REVIEW-LOG.md append-collision that breaks parallel droid work. Each droid owns its fragment.

column3: Each ticket's owns: is a single source of truth; depends_on: declares build-deps across tickets. Disjoint owns only rules out file collision, not deps.
column8: SLOP-TICKET: per-ticket owns/depends_on discipline — the disambiguation from 'disjoint owns is enough' to 'owns + depends_on both required at creation' is a Charon invention SLOP would benefit from.

column3: Capability self-test: parses the cost-tier registry at runtime and asserts the executor reads the SAME thresholds (no hardcoded duplicate).
column8: KSF-TICKET: gate-self-test pattern — a ksf module self-verifies that its own configuration is the one the executor reads, catching the 'drift between registry and consumer' class.
